'''Frank Reese Harvey''' (born 1941)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n88194277.html|title=Harvey, F. Reece|work=LC Name Authority File|publisher=Library of Congress|access-date=March 14, 2025}}</ref> is an American mathematician known for contributions to the field of [[differential geometry]]. In 1982, in collaboration with [[Blaine Lawson]], Harvey introduced [[calibrated geometry]], which is instrumental in the formulation of the [[SYZ conjecture]].<ref>{{cite book
 | last1 = Gross | first1 = Mark |author-link=Mark Gross (mathematician)
 | last2 = Huybrechts | first2 = Daniel |author-link2=Daniel Huybrechts
 | last3 = Joyce | first3 = Dominic |author-link3=Dominic Joyce
 | doi = 10.1007/978-3-642-19004-9
 | isbn = 3-540-44059-3
 | mr = 1963559
 | publisher = Springer-Verlag, Berlin
 | series = Universitext
 | title = Calabi-Yau Manifolds and Related Geometries: Lectures at a Summer School in Nordfjordeid, Norway, June 2001
 | year = 2003}} See p. 31 for credit for introducing calibrated geometry, definition 10.1, p. 50 for the connection between calibrations and the special Lagrangian submanifolds of the SYZ conjecture, and p. 64 for the formulation of the SYZ conjecture.</ref> He is Edgar Odell Lovett Professor and professor emeritus of mathematics at [[Rice University]],<ref name=9nas/>

==Education and career==
Harvey graduated from [[Carnegie Mellon University]] in 1963 with both a bachelor's and master's degree.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://profiles.rice.edu/faculty/f-reese-harvey|title=F. Reese Harvey|work=The People of Rice|publisher=Rice University|access-date=March 14, 2025}}</ref> He obtained his Ph.D. from [[Stanford University]] in 1966, under the direction of Hikosaburo Komatsu.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|33692}}</ref>

He joined the Rice University faculty in 1968, and retired as Edgar Odell Lovett Professor in 2003.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://naturalsciences.rice.edu/news/celebration-honors-f-reese-harveys-election-national-academy|title=Celebration honors F. Reese Harvey's election to National Academy|date=September 17, 2024|work=Natural Sciences News|publisher=Rice University Wiess School of Natural Sciences|access-date=March 14, 2025}}</ref>

==Recognition==
In 1983 he was an invited speaker at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Warsaw.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers?combine=harvey|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers|publisher=International Mathematical Union|access-date=2025-03-13}}</ref> In 2024, he was elected to the United States [[National Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=9nas>{{cite web|date=April 30, 2024|title=Nine mathematicians elected to National Academy of Sciences|website=[[American Mathematical Society]]|url=https://www.ams.org/news?news_id=7326}}</ref>
